items.name: Centring
items.formula: $x_i \to x_i - \bar x$; the rows of $X$ are the centred points
items.when: Always first: every variance in this course is spread around the mean $\bar x$.

items.name: Variance along a unit u
items.when: To score one direction from the points. $u$ must be a unit vector; this course divides by $n - 1$.

items.name: Total variance
items.when: Any direction and its perpendicular split this between them: along + across is always the total.

items.name: Covariance matrix
items.when: To get every variance at once. Row $i$, column $j$ of $X^\mathsf{T}X$ is (column $i$) · (column $j$); it equals its own transpose.

items.name: Variance from C
items.when: The variance along a unit $u$, straight from $C$ without going back to the points.

items.name: The best direction
items.when: The variance along $u$ is largest at $u = \pm v_1$, and there it equals $\lambda_1$.

items.name: Why nothing beats v₁
items.formula: $u = a v_1 + b v_2 \Rightarrow u^\mathsf{T}Cu = \lambda_1 a^2 + \lambda_2 b^2$
items.when: With $a^2 + b^2 = 1$ this is at most $\lambda_1$. $v_1 \perp v_2$ because $C$ is symmetric.

items.name: The closest line
items.formula: mean sq. distance to the line along $v_1$ $= \lambda_2$
items.when: The line with the most spread along it is the one closest to the points, measured perpendicular (not vertically, as in least squares).

items.name: Singular values and variances
items.when: $X^\mathsf{T}X = (n - 1)C$, so the SVD of the centred $X$ gives the PCA variances. Its right singular vectors $v_i$ are the principal directions.

items.name: Scores
items.when: Each point's one-number summary. Their squares add to $\sigma_1^2$.

items.name: Rebuilding a point
items.when: To read a point back from its score: the foot of $x_i$ on the line along $v_1$.

items.name: What one component loses
items.when: Eckart–Young: no rank-1 matrix is closer to $X$. Divided by $n - 1$ it is $\lambda_2$.

items.name: Explained variance ratio
items.when: To say how much of the spread one component keeps.
